families.name: Ordered rhythm
families.idea: A repeated span establishes order before additional shape or detail.
families.invariant: Retain the ordered landmarks and their repeat correspondence; equal spacing is an additional promise.

stages.label: One span
stages.caption: A directed span connects two distinct endpoint landmarks.

stages.label: Repeated chain
stages.caption: Corresponding spans continue through recurring landmarks.

stages.label: Aligned rows
stages.caption: Several chains add cross-row landmark correspondences.

families.name: Cross-lattice
families.idea: Two crossing line families create cells that can be grouped or selected.
families.invariant: Preserve the crossing incidence and cell adjacency; changing the view need not preserve angles or proportions.

stages.label: Crossing families
stages.caption: Two families of paths define a simple grid.

stages.label: Oblique view
stages.caption: The same incidence appears in a slanted representation.

stages.label: Selected cells
stages.caption: Grouped cells reveal a secondary pattern on the shared scaffold.

families.name: Selected-edge fret
families.idea: Selecting and interrupting lattice edges produces turns, returns and interlocking paths.
families.invariant: Retain path order and edge participation; a return on another level differs from retracing the same edge.

stages.label: One turn
stages.caption: A selected path turns on an exposed lattice.

stages.label: Stepped return
stages.caption: Repeated turns return along a distinct lane.

stages.label: Facing paths
stages.caption: Two selections occupy one scaffold without silently merging their identities.

families.name: Staggered repeat
families.idea: Neighbouring rows relate through an alternating placement phase.
families.invariant: A claimed half-drop needs a shared period: two half-shifts correspond to that whole period.

stages.label: Aligned repeat
stages.caption: Identical units recur in aligned rows.

stages.label: Alternating phase
stages.caption: Alternate rows shift through a declared half-period correspondence.

stages.label: Diamond scaffold
stages.caption: Neighbour connections reveal the staggered field's underlying skeleton.

families.name: Triangular compounds
families.idea: Shared triangular cells combine into lozenges, hexagons and stars.
families.invariant: Retain shared edges and compound-cell correspondence; equilateral lengths and turns require explicit additional promises.

stages.label: Triangular cell
stages.caption: Three edges close one cell with exposed shared-edge roles.

stages.label: Compound centre
stages.caption: Six triangular cells meet around one common centre.

stages.label: Selected field
stages.caption: Select hexagons and lozenges from a shared triangular scaffold.

families.name: Mixed-cell network
families.idea: Different boundary cycles cooperate to close the intervening field.
families.invariant: Account for the gap cells as well as the principal cells; local cycles alone do not prove a global tiling.

stages.label: One octagon
stages.caption: An eight-edge boundary encloses one cell.

stages.label: Intervening cells
stages.caption: Neighbouring octagons expose four-sided gaps that also need boundaries.

stages.label: Closed mixed field
stages.caption: Octagons and squares complete a repeated adjacency network.

families.name: Radial partition
families.idea: Rays and enclosing contours organize a field around a shared centre.
families.invariant: Retain the common centre, cyclic order and contour correspondence; equal angular sectors are a stronger promise.

stages.label: Shared centre
stages.caption: Several rays attach to the same actual centre.

stages.label: Closed sectors
stages.caption: A closed contour connects the rays in cyclic order.

stages.label: Sector bands
stages.caption: Nested contours cross the same radial structure to create related bands.

families.name: Independent-thread interlace
families.idea: Separate paths can cross while retaining independent continuity.
families.invariant: A projected crossing is not automatically a junction; over/under order belongs to an additional local relation.

stages.label: Two threads
stages.caption: One ordered crossing keeps two identifiable paths separate.

stages.label: Crossing order
stages.caption: Successive crossings expose a declared over/under sequence.

stages.label: Angular woven band
stages.caption: The crossing sequence repeats while each thread remains traceable.

families.name: Nested boundaries
families.idea: An enclosing boundary can contain bands, subordinate divisions and an inner court.
families.invariant: Retain containment and boundary adjacency; visual nesting alone does not establish equal gaps or scaling.

stages.label: Outer boundary
stages.caption: One closed boundary distinguishes an inside from its scoped surroundings.

stages.label: Inner court
stages.caption: A second boundary creates an intervening band and a retained centre.

stages.label: Subdivided bands
stages.caption: Additional divisions enrich the band without erasing its principal organization.

families.name: Counterchanged partition
families.idea: The occupied motif and intervening field can each support a coherent pattern reading.
families.invariant: Retain the common partition and an explicit role correspondence; equal significance does not imply equal physical area.

stages.label: Stepped division
stages.caption: A stepped boundary divides a bounded field into two regions.

stages.label: Two coherent roles
stages.caption: Repetition makes both the selected region and its complement legible.

stages.label: Role exchange
stages.caption: Exchange the roles through a supplied correspondence while retaining the partition.

goals.name: Continuous key
goals.why: A compact target for ordered turns, repeat continuity and legitimate returns.
must: The key path continues across the repeat boundary.
Returning paths use distinct occupied edges.
flexible: Stretch the key's proportions.
Vary the band and passage widths.
goals.miss: A convincing isolated key whose next repeat breaks the path or retraces an edge.

goals.name: Facing meanders
goals.why: Two related path systems frame a shared interior passage.
must: The two meanders retain distinct path identities.
Their inward-facing returns bound a recurring central passage.
flexible: Change the gap between the meanders.
Use longer or shallower returns.
goals.miss: Two unrelated rows that happen to sit near each other without a recurring facing relationship.

goals.name: Glide staircase
goals.why: A repeated stepped path exposes how reflection and displacement cooperate.
must: Neighbouring steps follow a declared reflection-and-displacement correspondence.
The resulting passages continue through the repeat.
flexible: Change the staircase's rise and run.
Change the separation of opposing steps.
goals.miss: An alternating staircase without a consistent glide correspondence between its repeated parts.

goals.name: Half-drop diamonds
goals.why: A sparse field makes phase, neighbourhood and repeat closure easy to inspect.
must: Alternate rows follow one shared half-period promise.
Both repeat directions preserve the declared neighbour correspondence.
flexible: Stretch the diamond proportions.
Change the gaps without changing neighbour order.
goals.miss: Rows appear staggered locally but drift out of phase when the field repeats.

goals.name: Nested diamond courts
goals.why: Nested courts combine enclosing cycles, radial correspondence and intervening passages.
must: Each court retains nested boundary cycles.
The intervening bands preserve their declared connections.
flexible: Vary court proportions and band widths.
Change the number of nested boundaries.
goals.miss: Nested outlines that collapse a required passage or lose their shared court correspondence.

goals.name: Triangular chambers
goals.why: A repeated triangular subdivision tests compound cells and subordinate enclosure.
must: The intended triangular chambers have closed boundaries.
Shared edges and enclosing bands retain their declared incidence.
flexible: Stretch triangles without changing incidence.
Change the depth of the enclosing bands.
goals.miss: A triangular-looking fragment whose chamber opens unintentionally at a neighbouring repeat.

goals.name: Octagon and square field
goals.why: The gap shapes become indispensable members of the repeated structure.
must: Eight-edge principal cells alternate with the intended four-edge gap cells.
Shared boundaries close across both repeat directions.
flexible: Vary edge lengths within compatible cells.
Exchange which cell family receives visual emphasis.
goals.miss: Octagons are repeated while the intervening gaps are omitted or left structurally unresolved.

goals.name: Counterchanged steps
goals.why: One stepped partition supports useful motif and field readings.
must: Both roles derive from the same bounded partition.
A supplied role-exchange correspondence preserves the intended adjacency.
flexible: Change the two roles' physical areas.
Stretch the steps while preserving their order.
goals.miss: Similar ink totals conceal different connectivity, or an empty complement is mistaken for a corresponding pattern.

goals.name: Angular woven band
goals.why: Independent continuity and local crossing order create complexity from a small path vocabulary.
must: Every thread remains traceable through each crossing.
The declared over/under sequence agrees at the repeat boundary.
flexible: Vary thread spacing and bend lengths.
Exchange the threads' visual emphasis.
goals.miss: A crossing silently merges two threads, or the crossing sequence contradicts itself on repetition.

goals.name: Herringbone passages
goals.why: Alternating slants produce a directional field with recurring angular passages.
must: Opposing slants recur in a consistent chevron sequence.
Passages and selected edges continue through neighbouring repeats.
flexible: Change the apparent lean.
Stretch the branches and intervening passages.
goals.miss: Locally attractive elbows accumulate inconsistent direction or disconnected passages across the field.

goals.name: Sixfold star corridors
goals.why: A shared radial organization can coordinate star centres and the corridors between them.
must: Each centre has six ordered corresponding sectors.
Neighbouring sector boundaries retain the intended corridor connections.
flexible: Vary the star's inner and outer reach.
Change corridor width under a compatible interpretation.
goals.miss: Six rays look balanced around isolated centres while their inter-centre corridors fail to connect.

goals.name: One scaffold two readings
goals.why: Alternative selections expose how one scaffold can support different coherent readings.
must: Both readings retain correspondence to one shared scaffold.
Their selected paths and complementary cells remain separately inspectable.
flexible: Choose different supported edge selections.
Change which reading is emphasized visually.
goals.miss: Two similar pictures are asserted to share a scaffold without a participant correspondence.
